description: Interactive standalone calculation practice tool for Grade 7 Mathematics — HCF Practice with Co-prime Detection. Five problems displayed as cards that students work through sequentially. Each card shows two numbers. Student enters the prime factorisation of each in an input area. The tool highlights matching primes with connecting lines between the two factorisations. Student selects minimum counts via dropdowns. The HCF is computed and validated. When HCF = 1, a special green CO-PRIME badge appears with a brief explanation. A progress bar at the top tracks completion. Emerald green (#10b981) accent for correct answers, rose for errors. Venn diagram overlay shows shared vs unique primes. Indian school context. Clean educational design using Lilita One + Nunito font family. Touch-friendly inputs for mobile. 5-colour palette: emerald, rose, white background, dark slate text, light grey card backgrounds.
topic: HCF When No Common Prime Factors and Practice
subject: Mathematics
curriculum: NCERT / Ganita Prakash — Chapter 3: Finding Common Ground
teachingNotes: Standalone practice tool — students work independently with immediate validation. Problem 3 (77, 725) is co-prime (HCF = 1). Problem 5 (81, 243) is special because 81 divides 243. Show a summary after all 5 are completed.
instructionsForStudent: For each pair of numbers, first find the prime factorisation of both. Then identify which primes are common. For each common prime, take the minimum count. Multiply them to get the HCF. Watch out for co-prime pairs where HCF = 1!
